# idamax

> Finds the index of the first element having maximum absolute value.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import idamax from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/idamax';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
idamax( N, x, strideX ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of elements in input vector(s) |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | storage spacing between elements of DX. |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `x` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: 0-based index of the max element, or -1 if N < 1

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
idamax.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX ) → integer
```

Finds the index of the first element having the maximum absolute value.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | strideX length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `x` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: 0-based index of the max element, or -1 if N < 1

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `idamax()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`IDAMAX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/idamax.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import idamax from './../lib/base.js';

// Find the index of the element with max absolute value:
const x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, -4.0, 3.0, 2.0 ] );

const idx = idamax( 4, x, 1, 0 );
console.log( idx ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 1
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `IDAMAX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

IDAMAX finds the index of the first element having maximum absolute value.

### Further Details

jack dongarra, linpack, 3/11/78. modified 3/93 to return if incx .le. 0. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
